name: FAST TRACK
description: Fast Track is a high-energy North American race game that combines card-driven movement with a physical board of marbles or pegs. Similar in spirit to Sorry! or Ludo, Fast Track replaces dice with each player's personal deck of cards. The goal is to navigate all four marbles around the track and into a central Home Base. The game features strategic mechanics like backwards-moving 4s, split 7s (move two marbles), and a dangerous central shortcut called the 'Fast Track' that saves board space but leaves marbles vulnerable.

content.text: Fast Track is a high-energy North American race game that combines card-driven movement with a physical board of marbles or pegs. Similar in spirit to Sorry! or Ludo, Fast Track replaces dice with each player's personal deck of cards. The goal is to navigate all four marbles around the track and into a central Home Base. The game features strategic mechanics like backwards-moving 4s, split 7s (move two marbles), and a dangerous central shortcut called the 'Fast Track' that saves board space but leaves marbles vulnerable.

Fast Track descends from the Aggravation and Wahoo family of race games, which themselves were adaptations of the English game Ludo. The card-based movement system emerged in the late 20th century as a DIY and homemade variant popular in Midwestern USA and Canada.
2 to 6 players (can be played in teams with partners sitting opposite each other on a square board).
Each player (or team) has their own full 52-card deck PLUS 2 Jokers (54 cards total per player deck). Keep decks separated by player.

1. **Fast Track Board**: Hexagonal or square board with 64-68 spaces around the perimeter plus 4 Home Base centers (one per player/team). 2. **Marbles or Pegs**: 4 marbles per player in their color. 3. **Holding Pen**: Off-board area where marbles start before being entered into play.
Each player shuffles their own deck and draws 5 cards into their starting hand. Place remaining cards face-down as draw pile.

items.text: Pegs and Jokers: Identical rules but played with wooden peg tracks and interlocking boards. The interlocking design creates a unique cross-pattern for 4-player games.
Tock (QuÃ©bÃ©cois Variant): Slight rule variations: 7 always means 7 steps (no split option). Jack values different card hierarchy. Popular in Quebec and Eastern Canada.
Dirty Marbles (Aggressive Variant): Bumping is MANDATORY whenever you land on an opponent. Creates chaos and more aggressive play.
Cooperative Fast Track: Teams work together to block a single opponent who starts with a head start. Last team standing wins.
Speed Variant: Players draw back to 10 cards instead of 5, speeding up play dramatically.
